Prevention: Plant disease free seedlings from certified nurseries such as
KALRO-Thika, JKUAT, Good neighbours and other
Plant seedlings grafted to brown spot tolerant yellow passion fruit rootstocks.
To improve aeration use recommended spacing of 3 metres between plants and 2 metres between rows.
Monitoring: Brown spots up to 10mm in diameter on the leaves extending along the veins and drying out in the centre.
Brown lesions on the stem that cause dieback when they occur at the leaf axils.
Spots that are light brown, round and sunken which often merge covering large areas and produce red brown spore masses.
Take immediate action once you see signs of the disease on one plant.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Remove and burn all infected plant parts.
Use drip irrigation and avoid overhead irrigation to reduce spread of pathogen.
Prune to promote proper orchard aeration and reduce disease build up.
Disinfect tools regulary e.g. by the use of jik solution 500ml in ten litres of water to prevent the spread of the fungus.
Direct Control (Chemical): When using pesticides always wear protective clothing
Always follow the instructions on the product label such as dosage, timing of application, PHI, maximum number of sprays, re
Always consult current list of registered pesticides
Carbendazim + Mancozeb based products such as
WP at the rate of 25g/ 20lts of water
Spray with copper based fungicides such as cupracaffaro at the rate of 50gm/20lts of water
WP 70 at the rate of 50ml/20lts of water
Spray with saaf and alternate with
Antracol after 7 days and repeat again untill the disease is controlled
Restrictions: IV; PHI 3 days; WHO Toxicity class
